start.speaker: Rosa
start.text: Hey — easy, the cherries roll. I'm Rosa. Twenty-two, Shake Row, crate hip, sundress, flip-flops, cherry toes. Mira's the neon; I'm the fruit and the trouble two stalls down. You buying, flirting, or lost?

who.speaker: Rosa
who.text: Rosa Velez. I haul fruit for the shakes Mira doesn't have time to garnish. Tía Mira says I'm loud. She's right. I grew up on this asphalt. Flip-flops are the uniform. Cherry polish is the rank.

tia.speaker: Rosa
tia.text: Not by blood. By Cool Down and by yelling. She keeps my sandals under her stool when I forget them, which is always. 'Go say hi if you like women who pour. Stay here if you like women who lean on crates.'

stall.speaker: Rosa
stall.text: Not a full shop yet. Crate, shade cloth, a chalkboard that says ROSA in pink. Cherries, mint Mira steals, sometimes a cup she 'accidentally' overpours. 'When I get a window, you'll know. Until then, you get me and the flip-flops.'

sample.speaker: Rosa
sample.text: Open. I hold it so you have to come in, thumb at my lip after like I didn't plan that. Sweet, a little mean. 'That's the row. Sticky. Worth it. You got juice on your mouth. I'm not wiping it unless you ask.'

flirt.speaker: Rosa
flirt.text: Direct. Cute. I pop a hip on the crate, sundress doing the Hwy 50 wind a favor, one flip-flop hanging off cherry toes. 'I get off when the neon does. Until then you can stand there and make me feel looked at. Fair?'

flirt_close.speaker: Rosa
flirt_close.text: Then come here. I tug your collar with two sticky fingers and don't kiss you — I almost do, which is worse. Vanilla from Mira's blender in the air. 'You smell like wilds. I like wilds on a person.'

almost.speaker: Rosa
almost.text: Kind is for church. This is Shake Row. I give you the corner of my mouth, cherry and laugh, then a flip-flop to the shin, light. 'Come back when my chalkboard says your name. I haven't decided the spelling.'

toes.speaker: Rosa
toes.text: Trap? It's a flip-flop, papi, not a spell. I kick it up, catch it with my toes, drop it, step back in. Cherry ten, dusty strap. 'Mira does gems. I do cheap and shiny. You can look. Everyone on 50 looks. You're just honest about it.'

toes_ok.speaker: Rosa
toes_ok.text: I do it again, slower, because I am not immune to a good audience. Dust on the sole, polish bright. 'Don't tell Deb. She'll put me on the diner special board.' I leave the flip-flop off a second longer than I need to.

choices.label: Put me on your chalkboard instead.

heat.speaker: Rosa
heat.text: Roasting. That's why the dress is thin and the flip-flops are optional. I fan myself with the chalkboard. 'Shade's mine if you share the crate. Feet up — tile burns. I already learned that the hard way, see?' Bare sole, a little dusty, still cute.

crate.speaker: Rosa
crate.text: We sit. Your shoulder, my knee, the row doing its noisy thing. I hook a heel on the crate edge and talk about nothing: cherries, Lila's cot, Yara making people hold a stance until they shake. 'This is my favorite shift. Nobody rushing. Somebody staying.'

choices.label: I have to hunt. I'll come back.

send_mira.speaker: Rosa
send_mira.text: Go on, the neon hut. Tell her Rosa wants extra ice and that I still have her spare sandals. She'll roll her eyes and make it anyway. Bring two if you want to sit on my crate after.

night.speaker: Rosa
night.text: When the neon dies I walk the lot in flip-flops and whatever's left of the sundress. Sometimes I end up on Mira's rail. Sometimes I end up here, crate as a bench, talking to somebody who didn't run. 'Be that somebody once.'

promise.speaker: Rosa
promise.text: Good. I'll save you a cherry and a look. Don't make me put your name on the board in mean letters. Go on — wilds, square, Mira, Lila, whoever. I'll be the flip-flops on Shake Row.

bye.speaker: Rosa
bye.text: Passing is allowed. Boring, but allowed. If you loop the row, I'm the sundress and the crate. Don't pretend you didn't see the cherry toes.
